title: No source fixes the field list of the plan-installment result or where its band and floor are held
source: _work/msr/context/S2.md (ownership rows of S2); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3.md (A2.6); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2.md (T3.1, T-A.1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E3-006 Data); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-01, R9)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; CON s3 Preconditions; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.7 Tables owned; s13
description: FEAT-TRT-06 produces the model installment and the range the officer may move within, and no source declares an object for the result. TSD S2 T3.1 gives the treatment only installment_amount (DF-TRT-031), installments (DF-TRT-009) and interest_rate (DF-TRT-027); it has no band, floor or payoff column. The ownership rows of the context pack give S2 one table, treatment, and no view and no data product. The legacy data table of RWB-E3-006 names recovery_case, v_ace_account, treatment, decision_log_entry, v_ace_score and rule_row, and every one of them belongs to another owner except treatment. FSD A2.6.3 carries validation rules only and, unlike A2.2, A2.3 and A2.4, no field catalog at all. The two stories therefore hold the result as the PlanInstallment element recorded against the treatment row plus the local decision record, and declare no new table, no new column and no migration.
evidence: Context pack S2 ownership rows: Tables (1) - treatment; Events (1) - EV-10; Jobs (0). TSD S2 T3.1 declares treatment with DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-014 and DF-TRT-023 to DF-TRT-033 and no band, floor or payoff object. FSD S2 A2.6.3 has A2.6.3.1 (validation rules) and A2.6.3.3 (roles) but no A2.6.3.2 field catalog, whereas A2.2.3.2 to A2.4.3.2 all carry one. Legacy RWB-E3-006 Data lists v_ace_account with DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042 and v_ace_score with DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279, neither of which is S2's.
area: Data model and contract, S2 rwb-treatment
owner_role: S2 rwb-treatment service owner and the P3 rwb-case reference-data owner
proposed: The service owner confirms the element at the wave 2 contract freeze. If a result table is wanted, the S2 DB story creates it on the service's own Flyway sequence and RWB-S2-E3006-CON declares its fields in a minor version; no behaviour and no dependency changes.

title: The reference set that holds the band, the floor and the freshness limit, and the operation that reads it, are not published
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-SET-01 to R-SET-05); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md (section 5.9); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2.md (T5.2, T-A.1); _work/msr/context/S2.md (ownership rows of S2); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R3 default rulings, R5.5 DP-07, R9)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; CON s3 Preconditions; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.5 Workflows and activities
description: R-SET-01 says the range is set from reference data, R-SET-03 tests payoff_as_at against the freshness limit, and R-SET-04 and R-SET-05 name settlement_range_low, settlement_range_high and floor_price, but no source names the reference set that holds those rows, its identifier, the operation that returns it, or the numeric value of the freshness limit. The owner is also stated twice: TSD S2 T5.2 routes reference data to P4, while the run's default rulings place parameters and reference data in P3 rwb-case and DP-07 names the reference-data contract of rwb-case. Both stories read through RWB-P3-E1043-CON and its client library against a fake, name the elements rather than an invented path, and let the set version travel on the element.
evidence: Routing Logic v4 R-SET-01 to R-SET-05 give the conditions and the three column names but no set identifier and no operation. TSD S2 T-A.1 lists four S2 operations and no reference read, and T5.2 states 'P4 for access and reference data'. Template and Rules R3 default rulings: Parameters and reference data (E1-042, E1-043) - P3 rwb-case; R5.5 DP-07: Reference data, LOV - Reference-data contract of rwb-case, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON.
area: Reference data and contract, S2 rwb-treatment against P3 rwb-case
owner_role: P3 rwb-case owner, with the P4 rwb-access owner confirming the superseded row
proposed: The run's default ruling stands: reference data is read from P3 rwb-case through RWB-P3-E1043-CON, and TSD S2 T5.2 is corrected in its next version. The set identifiers, the four values and the freshness limit are published as rows before the wave 2 tag; RWB-S2-E3006-CON then names them in a minor version.

title: No requirement ID is allocated to FEAT-TRT-06
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2.md (T8); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md (section 5.9); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md (feature row FEAT-TRT-06); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R9)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s18 Traceability; CON s2 Business rationale; s18 Traceability
description: TSD S2 T8 maps REQ-S2-001 to REQ-S2-010 to FEAT-TRT-01 only, and the Program BRD section 5.9 carries ten requirements of which none names FEAT-TRT-06. The two section 5.9 requirements that describe the surrounding outcome, REQ-S2-001 (a restructure reaching the officer with the case) and REQ-S2-004 (terms negotiated inside a rule-set range), name no feature. The trace of both stories therefore runs on the feature code FEAT-TRT-06 until the C1 PRD allocates a requirement, and no requirement ID is invented.
evidence: TSD S2 T8 rows REQ-S2-001 to REQ-S2-010 all read FEAT-TRT-01 in the Feature column. Business Requirements Program section 5.9 lists REQ-S2-001 to REQ-S2-010 with no feature column. The Epics 3 to 8 feature sheet row E3, S2, FEAT-TRT-06 carries a kind, a role, systems and a dependency but no requirement ID.
owner_role: Programme business analyst and the PRD owner of the S2 PRD
proposed: The C1 PRD allocates a requirement to FEAT-TRT-06, the RTM adds the row, and both story files take the ID in a minor version; no acceptance criterion changes.

title: Architecture v5 says the recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data while DP-05 allows the service's own views
source: _work/msr/context/S2.md (Architecture v5 slide 8 notes and the DP table in short form); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-05, R3 source precedence); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3.md (A2.6.3.1 VR-S2-006-1, A1.1 constraints)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s12.7 Tables owned; s17 Guardrails; CON s3 Preconditions; s12.5 Workflows and activities; s12.9 Call-type summary
description: Architecture v5 slide 8 says the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data, and the FSD's re-base under D-RCV-35 says source data is read only through those views. DP-05 allows two paths: rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views. The Work Package records no contract dependency on P1, so the second path is the only one that lets the story start on Day 1, and it needs SELECT on two views granted to this service's login. The stories read recovery.v_ace_account and recovery.v_ace_batch_status only, at the ACE batch date, with no copy and no third ACE object.
evidence: Context pack, slide 8 notes: 'ACE schemas and the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views (read only by rwb-source-data)'. Template and Rules DP-05: 'AceSourceQuery, v_ace_*, account_ext - Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views - none'. FSD S2 A2.6.3.1 VR-S2-006-1 tests v_ace_batch_status, which is one of the views in question. The Work Package lists C RWB-P3-E1043-CON and no P1 contract story.
area: Data access and security, ACE database
owner_role: ACE DB owner, with the P1 rwb-source-data owner and the platform data owner
proposed: Grant SELECT on the two views to the rwb-treatment login before the wave 2 tag. If the grant is refused, the read moves to the rwb-source-data contract in a minor version of RWB-S2-E3006-CON and the Work Package records the C dependency on the P1 contract story.

title: The FSD does not say whether the range the officer may move within is an amount band or an installment range
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3.md (A2.6.1, A2.6.2); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-SET-01, R-SET-04, R-SET-05); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E3-006 AC1); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R9)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s8 Business rules; CON s3 Preconditions; s12.1 REST operations provided
description: The feature objective says it produces the model installment and the range the officer may move within, without saying whether the range is an amount band or a range of installments. R-SET-04 and R-SET-05 test offer_amount against settlement_range_low, settlement_range_high and floor_price, which are amount tests, and R-SET-01 sets the range from reference data at the same step that calculates the payoff. The element therefore carries the band and the floor as amounts, and the installment figures as the model installment and the count, so a reader can derive an installment range without a second definition.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.6.1 and A2.6.2 give the objective sentence only and no field, unit or example. Routing Logic v4 R-SET-04: offer_amount between settlement_range_low and settlement_range_high; R-SET-05: offer_amount < floor_price. Legacy RWB-E3-006 AC1 names no unit.
owner_role: Business lead of S2 and the P3 rwb-case reference-data owner
proposed: The business lead confirms the unit at the wave 2 contract freeze. If an installment range is wanted, the element gains two optional fields in a compatible change and no acceptance criterion changes.

title: No source names the trigger of the plan-installment step
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3.md (A2.6.2, A2.6.4.4); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E3-006 AC1, AC2); _work/msr/context/S2.md (ownership rows of S2, slide 13 matrix)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow; s7 Acceptance criteria; s12.4 Events consumed; CON s3 Preconditions; s12.5 Workflows and activities
description: FSD A2.6.2 gives the trigger as 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer' and A2.6.4.4 records no background event, so no source says which of the three starts the step, and no event is named for it. AC2 of the legacy key ties the settlement branch to R-SET-01 and the ROUTE_APPROVED event on the case, while AC1, one of the two criteria this story owns, names only 'its trigger'. The stories therefore treat the trigger as the case signal the parent CaseWorkflow forwards to the stage, and publish no Kafka subscription of their own for it.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.6.2 step 1: 'Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'. FSD S2 A2.6.4.4: 'None - No background event'. Legacy RWB-E3-006 AC1: 'When its trigger arrives'. Context pack: Jobs (0), and the slide 13 matrix shows P3 Case starting the interaction with S2 by Temporal and event.
owner_role: S2 rwb-treatment service owner and the P3 rwb-case workflow owner
proposed: The case workflow owner confirms the signal at the wave 2 contract freeze. If a Kafka event is wanted instead, it is added to the consumed list of RWB-S2-E3006-CON in a minor version and the branch is started by that event with no change to the element.

title: AC2 of RWB-E3-006 is owned by no story of this Work Package
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/aisdlc/_work/msr/wp/B2-S2-001.md (story lines); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E3-006 AC2); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-SET-01)
section: APP s1 Story; s7 Acceptance criteria; s16 Test cases; s19 Out of scope; CON s7 Acceptance criteria; s16 Test cases; s19 Out of scope
description: The Work Package gives RWB-S2-E3006-APP the criteria AC1 and AC3 and gives RWB-S2-E3006-CON none, so AC2 of the legacy key, the R-SET-01 step from ROUTE_APPROVED_SETTLEMENT to PAYOFF_AND_RANGE_SET, is owned by no story in this Work Package. Both stories say so in their scope statements and neither renumbers the criterion or its test case TC-E3-006-02, so the register can attribute it when the settlement stories of this service are checked.
evidence: Work Package B2-S2-001 story line RWB-S2-E3006-APP lists acs AC1 and AC3 only; the CON line lists acs [] . Legacy RWB-E3-006 AC2 is 'Rule R-SET-01' with its state move; TC-E3-006-02 covers it.
owner_role: S2 rwb-treatment service owner and the story set coordinator
proposed: The coordinator attributes AC2 and TC-E3-006-02 to the settlement state story of this service in the Service Story Catalog; if that story does not exist, a delta story is raised for it and no file of this Work Package changes.
